description: AI-powered Mission Control console that solves one of NASA’s greatest engineering bottlenecks for permanent lunar exploration: safely connecting sunlit solar ridges to ice-rich Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) at the Lunar South Pole. By fusing real NASA Moon Trek spatial imagery, three specialized TensorFlow neural networks, and an interactive 3D terrain & shadow CAD inspector, it empowers mission planners to pinpoint safe habitat pads and plot obstacle-free power and water supply routes.
summary:
Zero-Point Lunar is an AI-powered Mission Control console for NASA’s Artemis program that helps astronauts safely build a base at Shackleton Crater (89.9 degrees South) on the Lunar South Pole.

What It Does

Finds Safe Routes: Uses real NASA Moon Trek imagery to map obstacle-free paths between sunny solar power ridges ("Peaks of Eternal Light") and dark, ice-filled craters (PSRs), dodging steep cliffs over 18 degrees.

Scans Landing Sites with AI: Runs three TensorFlow models on lunar satellite photos to detect flat landing pads (under 5 degrees), score cryogenic freeze risks (-240 degrees Celsius), and pinpoint GPS-denied coordinates.

Simulates 3D Terrain & Landings: Uses Three.js WebGL and NASA elevation data to render interactive 3D crater terrain with live polar sun shadows and rocket descent telemetry.

Why It Matters
It turns weeks of manual NASA data cross-referencing into instant engineering decisions—preventing lander tip-overs and hardware freeze traps to accelerate permanent human life on the Moon.
details:
AI-powered Mission Control platform for NASA’s Artemis program, built to safely connect sunlit solar ridges ("Peaks of Eternal Light") to ice-rich Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs) at Shackleton Crater on the Lunar South Pole.

How It Works

  • Solar-to-Ice Pathfinder: Uses NASA Moon Trek LRO imagery to plot obstacle-free supply routes between solar power peaks and water-ice craters, avoiding slopes over $18^\circ$.
  • 3-Model AI Habitat Scanner: Runs TensorFlow/Keras neural networks on LRO orbital cutouts to classify safe landing pads, calculate cryogenic freeze risks, and lock GPS-denied crater coordinates.
  • 3D Topography & Descent Simulator: Renders interactive Three.js WebGL terrain from LOLA elevation data with real-time polar sun-angle shadow simulation and rocket terminal descent telemetry.

Impact & Benefits Compresses weeks of manual site-selection cross-referencing into real-time engineering decisions—preventing lander tip-overs, boulder damage, and hardware freeze traps to accelerate permanent lunar habitation.

Tech Stack & NASA Data

  • Code & Libraries: Python, Flask, TensorFlow/Keras, Three.js (WebGL), Leaflet.js, Apache ECharts, HTML5/CSS3/JS.
  • NASA Data: NASA Moon Trek WMTS LRO Global Mosaic, LROC WAC/NAC imagery, LOLA Digital Elevation Models, and Diviner thermal data.
